relatedSnapshot.title: Billing card shows CMR-ended domains as Active while they are still billed
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

The CMR domain audit marks a domain `overcharged` when CMR has ended it but Autumn/Whop billing still renews (e.g. a domain cancelled in CMR on Sep 25 with inbox billing still renewing Oct 25).

The **customer** billing card had no case for `overcharged`, so those domains showed:

* no billing badge
* inboxes labelled **Active**
* a **"Payment due"** countdown

So a customer paying for a domain that no longer exists saw the opposite of the truth, with no signal that anything was wrong. The admin side has flagged this since ENG-14258; the customer side never did.

## Solution

* `DomainBillingBadge`: `overcharged` renders **"Ended <date> · Still billed"** (warning) with a tooltip telling the customer to cancel to stop billing.
* New `isOverchargedDomainBilling` and `isEndedDomainBilling` helpers.
* `EmailAccountsDomainsCard`: for ended domains (inactive or overcharged), inboxes show **"Ended"** and the payment-due column is hidden.
* The **Cancel button stays** for overcharged domains — `cancelManagedDomainInProvider` already treats CMR "already cancelled / not found" as success, so cancelling proceeds to cancel the billing. This is the customer's self-serve fix.

## Regression guard

Adds a test that **every** audit payment state renders a badge except the internal `unlinked` and `error`, so a newly added state cannot silently render nothing again — which is exactly how this bug arose when `overcharged` was introduced.

## Testing

* `bunx vitest run tests/components/billing/domain-billing-badge.test.tsx` — 11 passed.
* Biome, tsc on changed files, `check-v2 --changed` clean.

## Coordination note

Acquisity/Acquisity#6642 (ENG-14340) also edits `email-accounts-domains-card.tsx` and is still open. The two are logically consistent — ENG-14340 hides Cancel for `cmr_inactive` (nothing left to cancel), this one deliberately keeps it for `overcharged` (billing is still running, so cancelling is the fix) — but they will likely conflict in that file. Worth landing them in a deliberate order.

## Notes

3 files, +55/-4. Part of the CMR domain audit series.

## Customer report

```text
This is a billing dispute for the billing team to reconcile. It is not a refund request yet, and nothing has been promised to the customer.

What the customer reports: Their campaign shows 15 inboxes, but 3 inboxes under <domain> are not in the campaign. Their Billing screen shows those inboxes in Error, with a payment due today (screenshot reading: "Normal · Error · Added September 14, 2026"). They say they have no idea what is going on, and they asked for a human agent. Support already had them check the Email Accounts page: all 15 listed inboxes are Active with 100% health, so the connected ones are fine. The customer did not say which charge they dispute beyond the inboxes now showing payment due.

What the results show:
- One done-for-you order, created 2026-09-14, records a paid date of 2026-09-14 20:56. Its status is requires_attention and it stopped at step 5/6. It reconciles to 6 domains and 18 inboxes charged, but 5 domains and 15 inboxes provisioned and connected. 1 domain failed and 3 inboxes are missing. A provisioning failure was recorded on 2026-09-28 with the message "Provisioned 5/6 domains, 15/18 inboxes". The order's technical error details are unavailable. No retry attempts are recorded (provisioningAttempts 0).
- The 6 domains in the order are <domain>, <domain>, <domain>, <domain>, <domain> and <domain>. I could not confirm from the results which of the six failed. The customer's screenshot and the earlier team notes point to <domain>.
- A paid invoice on 2026-09-14 for $198.26 (charge succeeded) lists 6 yearly domain lines ($11.46, $16.74, $14.29, $16.74, $14.29, $16.74) and inbox lines at $18.00 per month for 3 inboxes each, covering 2026-09-14 to 2026-10-14. The invoice lines are truncated, so I only saw 4 of the 6 inbox lines. No source ties this charge to the order, so payment for the order itself is unconfirmed. The invoice and the order both show 6 domains.
- Billing shows an active subscription for every one of the 6 domains and all 6 inbox groups, including <domain> inboxes, even though 3 inboxes on this order were not provisioned. The inbox allowance shows 18 granted, 15 used, 3 unused. The domain allowance shows 6 granted, 5 used, 1 unused.
- The inbox billing period from the 2026-09-14 invoice ended on 2026-10-14, which matches the customer seeing payment due today. The next inbox renewal, including the 3 undelivered inboxes, has not been confirmed as charged.
- The reconciliation note says Stripe shows a succeeded charge but the product database has no active subscription status for the organization. It should be checked for charged-but-not-provisioned.
- No refunds are recorded and there are no failed payments. The other recent charges are the Pro plan ($185 on 2026-09-14 and on 2026-10-14) and 50,000 credits ($300 on 2026-09-15). The customer has not disputed these.

What billing needs to do: reconcile what the customer was charged against what was delivered. Decide how to treat the missing domain and 3 inboxes, and whether the renewal due today should be charged for inboxes that were never set up. Also check whether provisioning for the failed domain should be re-run. The customer must not be asked to place a new order or pay again while this is unresolved.
```

relatedSnapshot.title: Domains in failed/Error state have no Cancel option, leaving active inboxes uncancellable
relatedSnapshot.description:
BUG: Yes

EVIDENCE:

* Customer: Name 2 (<email>), workspace **Company One** (`<workspace-slug>`, org `<uuid>`). Reports domains/inboxes still active after cancelling, and no Cancel button in Settings -> Billing -> Email Accounts & Domains.
* Prod DB: Company One has 12 `mail_domain` rows across 2 DFY orders.
  * 6 are `suspended` / "Cancelled by user" (updated 2026-07-20 14:36) - his cancellation on Jul 20 worked for these.
  * 6 are `failed` / "Name 3 waiting for domain/mailboxes": `<domain>`, `<domain>`, `<domain>`, `<domain>`, `<domain>`, `<domain>`.
* Those failed domains still have **15** `mail_inbox` **rows with** `status = active`**,** `connected = true` (3 per domain; the 3 on <domain> are already `error`). Provisioning was recorded as failed at the domain level but the mailboxes exist and are live.
* Root cause in UI: `apps/web/components/billing/email-accounts-domains-card.tsx:44` - `const CANCELLABLE_DOMAIN_STATUSES = ['pending', 'active', 'partial']`. Domains with status `failed` render as "Error" but `isCancellable` is false, so there is no per-domain **Cancel** button and they are excluded from **Cancel all**. No self-serve path exists to remove them or their still-live inboxes.
* Orders: `<uuid>` (status `completed`, "Provisioned 2/6 domains, 6/18 inboxes") and `<uuid>` (status `requires_attention`, "Provisioned 4/6 domains, 12/18 inboxes").
* Billing (Autumn customer `<uuid>` / Stripe `<stripe-id>`): products `Domain` (qty 12) and `Inbox (DFY)` (qty 12) are `past_due` with `canceled_at = 2026-07-20`, current period end **2026-08-18**. $108/mo charge attempts have been failing since 2026-07-18 (8 declines through 2026-07-29).
* Separate question in the same conversation: the **$297 charged 2026-07-27** is the monthly **Pro** plan on a different workspace, **"Test 1"** (`<workspace-slug>`, billing account `<uuid>`, Stripe `<stripe-id>`), billed monthly since 2025-11-27. Not an Company One charge.

POTENTIAL FIX:

* Make provisioning-`failed` domains removable: either add `failed` to `CANCELLABLE_DOMAIN_STATUSES` with a cancel path that also tears down inboxes still `active`/`connected` under that domain, or surface a distinct "Remove" action for error-state domains.
* Reconcile domain vs inbox state: a `failed` domain should not keep `active`, `connected` inboxes. Add a reconciliation job plus a backfill for existing rows.

WHATS NEEDED TO RESOLVE:

* Engineering decision on the cancel/removal path for `failed` domains.
* Manual cleanup for Company One now: remove the 6 failed domains and their 15 active inboxes.
* Confirm no further billing for Company One after 2026-08-18.
* Reply to the customer on the $297 charge (Pro plan on the "Test 1" workspace).

DOCS GAP: The Help Center billing docs (`apps/web/content/docs/workspace-settings/billing.mdx`, "Email Accounts & Domains") describe **Cancel** / **Cancel all** but never explain that domains in an **Error** state show no Cancel button, why, or that support must remove them. Fin AI gave the customer cancel steps he could not follow before handing off.
CUSTOMER CONTEXT: Customer tried to cancel his workspace, emails and domains; the remaining billed items were error-state domains with no Cancel control, so he assumed cancellation had not worked.
SUGGESTED CONTENT: Add an FAQ - "Why is there no Cancel option next to my domain?" - covering the Error/failed provisioning state, its billing impact, and how to get it removed. Also add a note that each workspace bills separately and how to identify which workspace a charge belongs to.
RELATED DOC(S): <url:app.acquisity.ai>

INTERCOM: <url:app.intercom.com>
SLACK THREAD: <url:acquisityworkspace.slack.com>
DEVIN SESSION: <url>

When a domain ends at the supplier, stop billing it and help the customer replace it
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Some domains end at the supplier while the customer is still paying for them: pre-warmed domains that reach their expiry, and domains the supplier has cancelled. The customer should be warned 30 days ahead, offered replacement mailboxes, and never charged after the end date. Today about 700 ended domains are still being billed.

## Problem

* Pre-warmed domains cannot be renewed with the supplier, and they expire before the customer's yearly billing date because they were registered as stock before purchase. We don't store supplier expiry dates, so nobody is warned.
* When a domain ends at the supplier, our billing keeps charging for it and its mailboxes. On 28 Sep the audit showed 692 such domains across 146 workspaces (about 1,710 mailboxes). The billing page shows "Ended, still billed", but the customer has to cancel it themselves.
* Customers find out when their campaigns stop sending, then open refund tickets.

## User experience

* 30 days and 7 days before a pre-warmed domain ends: email and in-app notice to the workspace Owner and Admins: "{domain} and its 3 mailboxes stop working on {date}. Replace them now to keep sending." Button: Buy replacement mailboxes.
* Billing shows "Active until {date}" on these domains instead of a renewal.
* On the end date, or as soon as the supplier ends a domain: billing for it and its mailboxes stops automatically, and the customer gets "{domain} has ended. You won't be charged for it again."

No email or screen names the supplier.

## What's included

* Use the purchase and end dates stored and synced daily by ENG-14462 (split out on 29 Sep 2026).
* The 30 and 7 day warnings with a working replacement purchase link.
* Automatic billing stop for ended domains through the shared cancel routine in ENG-14252.
* Stop any yearly charge for a pre-warmed domain that will not exist for that year.
* The refund decision and a one-off cleanup of the domains overcharged today, with a dry-run list first. The cleanup is a production billing change and needs its own go.

Not included: renewing done-for-you domains, which is ENG-13745.

## Blocked by

* ENG-14252

## Done when

- [ ] Every live pre-warmed domain shows its real end date in Billing.
- [ ] A test pre-warmed domain 30 days from expiry triggers the warning with a working replacement link.
- [ ] A domain ended at the supplier stops billing within a day, with no customer action.
- [ ] The overcharged count in the domain audit falls to zero, apart from findings under review.

## Open questions

* Refunds for charges made after the end date: account credit or cash? Recommended: credit by default, cash on request.

## Implementation context

* The supplier's domain list already returns an expiry date, but no table keeps it. `mail_domain.expires_at` exists and is only written by the Name 5 renewal webhook.
* The order row (`domain_purchase_order.order_type`) says pre-warmed or done-for-you; the domain row itself does not.
* The audit already marks ended-but-billed domains `overcharged` (ENG-14258), and the billing card shows it (ENG-14374). Admins currently cannot cancel `overcharged` findings from the audit.
* Related: ENG-14187 (unconnected pre-warmed seats stay billed).

relatedSnapshot.title: Let workspace owners load the Domain Management card on the Billing page
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

The Domain Management card on the Billing page never loads for the owners of a workspace, so it shows "Domains could not be loaded." instead of their purchased domains. Every owner who is not a platform admin is locked out of that card, and Retry never helps.

## Problem

An owner opens Settings, then Billing, to review purchase and renewal costs for their purchased website domains. The card renders an error with a Retry button that cannot succeed. They cannot see the domain list, its renewal settings or its links into the Name 6 from that surface, and the same failure has been reported repeatedly since late September. Nothing tells them whether the problem is theirs, ours, or their billing.

## Root cause

`apps/web/trpc/routers/website/owned-domain-management-procedures.ts` `listOwnedDomains` gates the billing summary on `canViewWebsiteDomainBillingSummary` (`apps/web/lib/website/owned-domain-management.ts`, lines 74 to 94) and throws FORBIDDEN with "Only organization owners can view domain billing details." when it returns false. That helper only accepts a caller whose platform user role is `admin` or `superadmin`, or one who appears in `organization.members` with the role `owner`. The organization object the procedure passes in comes from `assertUserIsOrgMemberOrAdmin` and then `assertUserIsOrgMember`, and the normal signed-in path returns `OrganizationMembershipSummary` from `apps/web/lib/auth/organization-membership.ts`, which carries only id, name, partnerId, slug and billingAccountId. It has no `members` array, so the check is always false for an owner whose platform role is `user`, which is every ordinary workspace owner. The member role the check needs is already resolved on that path and simply is not passed to the helper.

The unit tests for the helper pass a hand-built organization that does have a `members` array, so the suite stays green while production fails.

## Blast radius

Confirmed affected: 1,818 events across 190 organizations and 178 users between 13 and 16 October 2026, all of them with platform role `user` and not impersonated, counted 16 October 2026 with Axiom: `['acquisity'] | where tostring(fields.errorMessage) == "Only organization owners can view domain billing details." | summarize events=count(), orgs=dcount(tostring(fields.organizationId)), users=dcount(tostring(fields.userId)) by bin(_time,1d)`. The log window starts 13 October, so the figure is a floor rather than a start date, and it grew during the investigation. The Sentry issue ACQUISITY-4Z2 carries the same message on `GET /api/trpc/website.domainMarketplace.listOwnedDomains`, unresolved, at about 300 users and 1,292 events since roughly 22 September 2026; that read could not be repeated during review, so treat the Sentry figures as unverified.

Potentially exposed: every workspace with the Name 6 Creator feature whose owner opens Settings, then Billing, because the card renders for all of them. Not counted, because nothing separates "card rendered for an owner" from "card loaded".

## Proposed fix

Make the billing-summary gate read the caller's membership from the source the authorization path already resolved, or pass the resolved member role into the helper, so an owner whose platform role is `user` passes. Keep the gate itself intact: only owners and admins may see billing details, and members and customer-success sessions must keep being refused.

## What's included

In scope: the gate fix in the owned-domain path and a regression test that exercises it with the organization shape the signed-in authorization path really returns. Out of scope: who is allowed to see billing details, the domain purchase, refund and audit flows, and the other owner-only reads that were not investigated here. No separate containment, recovery, prevention or observability work is filed: no data, money or domain state is harmed by this failure, and the same domains stay reachable from the Name 6's own domains list, which calls the procedure without the billing summary.

Related, not part of this cause: a refunded Done-For-You order in the reporting workspace went on to have its mailboxes connected, which is the pattern owned by ENG-14716.

## Regression seam

`listOwnedDomains` called with `includeBillingSummary: true` by a signed-in workspace owner. Red before: the call throws FORBIDDEN with "Only organization owners can view domain billing details.". Green after: the call returns the workspace's domain list.

## Done when

* An owner whose platform role is `user` loads the Domain Management card on Settings, then Billing, and sees their domains.
* The FORBIDDEN count for callers with platform role `user` on this procedure falls to zero in production.
* A regression test proves the gate at the seam above, using the organization shape `assertUserIsOrgMember` returns rather than a hand-built object with a `members` array.

## Reports

* ENG-15585 Support chat after hours: the customer asked for a person

relatedSnapshot.title: Cancelling domains always stops every charge, and never cancels anything else
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When a customer, an admin or an automated job cancels domains, every matching domain and mailbox charge must stop at the end of the paid period, and nothing else on the account may be touched. Today a bulk cancel can stop partway and keep charging, and a fallback can cancel the wrong subscription, including the customer's main plan. This ticket builds the one cancel routine every other billing ticket in ENG-13358 reuses.

## Problem

* A customer cancels all their domains. Our records mark everything cancelled, but the billing side stops at the first error or the 5 minute request limit, so the rest keep renewing. The cancelled domains disappear from the page, so the customer cannot retry. 41 workspaces were affected (about 80 domains and 392 mailboxes, roughly $3,136 a month, estimated and not checked against invoices).
* If the first billing call finds no matching subscription, a fallback picks any active subscription on the customer, which can be the main plan.
* The supplier is cancelled immediately, which switches the mailboxes off straight away, while our billing runs to the end of the period. The customer loses service they have paid for.
* Legacy add-ons that cover several domains cannot be targeted, so they keep billing.

Found by the code audit on 28 Sep and not yet reproduced (verify first):

* Whop cancels can report an error after the supplier was already cancelled, so the customer sees a failure and Whop keeps charging.
* A domain whose billing provider differs from the workspace's is cancelled at the supplier, but its billing is skipped while the page shows success.
* Mailbox billing is silently skipped when the order type can't be worked out.
* A partial cancel updates the remaining mailbox count without naming a subscription, which may overbill.
* Cancelling an order with no domains can cancel the whole domain and mailbox products.

## User experience

* A customer cancels one domain or uses "Cancel all". Each domain keeps working and shows "Cancels on {date}" until its paid period ends, then stops. The customer is never charged for it again. The confirm dialog says this, instead of "stop sending immediately".
* If billing cannot be stopped for a domain, the domain stays visible as "Cancellation pending" and we retry automatically. Support sees it in the admin view.
* Nothing on the account other than the selected domains and their mailboxes changes.

## What's included

* One cancel routine used by every cancel path: customer, admin, and the automated tickets in this programme. Each domain's billing cancel is its own retried step with its own saved status, so one failure never blocks the rest and a retry resumes where it stopped.
* Supplier side: switch renewal off with the supplier through a new renewal on/off call, verified in the supplier sandbox first, so the mailboxes run to the end of the paid month. Remove them from sending and mark them cancelled only once the supplier confirms they ended. The immediate supplier cancel stays available for explicit admin use only.
* Find each domain's billing subscription by product, not by a constructed id. Legacy add-ons that cover several domains get a quantity reduction instead of a cancel.
* Remove the fallback that can cancel any subscription.
* Whop and mixed-provider domains follow the same saved-status rules.
* A daily comparison of live billing add-ons against cancelled domains that alerts on any stray add-on.
* Verify and fix the suspected problems listed above.
* Check ENG-13350 (customers get a "something went wrong" error when cancelling inboxes and domains). It is likely the same cancel path; fix it here or record why it is different.

Not included: the one-off cleanup of the remaining stray add-ons, which is listed on the master and needs its own go.

## Blocked by

None: can start immediately.

## Done when

- [ ] Cancelling 12 domains where the 6th billing call fails still stops billing for the other 11, and the 6th is retried and completes.
- [ ] A cancelled domain keeps sending until its paid month ends, then stops, and the supplier shows renewal off.
- [ ] No code path can cancel a subscription that is not the selected domain's or mailbox's.
- [ ] A Whop cancel never reports failure after the supplier was cancelled.
- [ ] The daily comparison finds zero stray add-ons for cancelled domains on a test account.
- [ ] Tests cover partial failure, retry, legacy multi-domain add-ons, Whop and mixed providers.

## Reports

* Intercom conversation, 24 Sep: the owner removed all 6 domains and 18 mailboxes before the cycle and was still charged. Production showed every row cancelled while the billing provider still listed 3 domain and 4 mailbox add-ons with no cancellation, and the renewal invoice charged the 4 mailbox add-ons. Refund: ENG-14253.
* A read-only sweep of 548 billing customers on 28 Sep found 134 add-ons still billing after a customer cancel. 122 were cancelled at end of cycle that day and verified. Still open: 12 add-ons on 2 accounts blocked by an expired Stripe discount; 102 legacy add-ons on accounts with live domains that need a quantity reduction; 50 add-ons on failed domains and 83 on moved domains still billing; 4 add-ons for live domains wrongly scheduled to cancel.
* Replaces ENG-14256, which counted 449 workspaces that had cancelled every domain (3,163 domain and 9,124 mailbox rows) as of 25 Sep.

## Implementation context

* `cancelManagedDomains` (`apps/web/lib/billing/email-management.ts`) marks rows cancelled before the billing adjustment and turns a billing failure into `billingAdjustmentStatus: 'failed'` while still returning success.
* `applyAutumnEndOfCycleCancellation` (`apps/web/lib/billing/providers/autumn/managed-domain-cancellation.ts`) walks domains in a plain sequential loop with no per-domain isolation or retry. The any-subscription fallback is in the same file.
* `getManagedDomainsForCancellation` only returns pending, active or partial domains, so cancelled rows cannot be targeted again.
* Recommended shape: an Inngest job with one retried step per add-on and a per-domain billing-cancel status.
* Existing test harness: `apps/web/tests/lib/billing/email-management-cancel-managed-domains.test.ts`.
* Investigation notes, affected-owner list and the 28 Sep cancel log were produced during the 28 Sep investigation and can be attached on request.

relatedSnapshot.title: Flag inactive CMR domains that are still billed as overcharged
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

Since Acquisity/Acquisity#6595, the CMR Domain Subscription Audit records domains that are INACTIVE or EXPIRED at ColdMailReseller as `cmr_inactive`. It doesn't check whether the customer is still being billed for them, so a customer paying for a domain that no longer exists at CMR looks identical to one who stopped paying.

There is also a quieter bug: a dedicated billing subscription for an inactive domain went into the group's shared pool and could count as coverage for an active domain, hiding an unpaid active domain.

## Root cause

Classification only matched billing subscriptions against active domains. Anything attached to an inactive domain was treated as unmatched pool coverage, and inactive domains were never compared against billing.

## Solution

* Match subscriptions against every domain in a billing group. A subscription dedicated to an inactive domain stays with that domain and no longer covers active ones.
* New payment state `overcharged` for an inactive domain that is still billed. It applies when either:
  * its dedicated domain/inbox subscription is active and not scheduled to end, or
  * pooled (unmatched) billing covers more domains/inboxes than the group's active domains need. Surplus is assigned to inactive domains alphabetically: one domain each, inboxes up to each domain's inbox count. If the surplus comes from the billing feature ledger, the note says it may include comped grants.
* Billing already scheduled to end is not flagged. The domain stays `cmr_inactive` with "billing ends YYYY-MM-DD" in the note.
* Groups where every domain is inactive now get a billing lookup (Acquisity/Acquisity#6595 skipped this).
* `overcharged` has severity 3, is included in "Action needed", the run summary's actionable list, and a new "Overcharged" tab with an amber badge. It is not a CMR-cancellable state (the domain is already dead at CMR; the fix is on the billing side) but it can be dismissed.
* Migration widens `cmr_domain_audit_finding_payment_state_check` with `overcharged` using `NOT VALID` then `VALIDATE`, following Acquisity/Acquisity#6595.

## Impact

* **User:** none directly. Admins can now find customers paying for dead domains and refund/cancel that billing.
* **Business:** catches overbilling before it becomes a support ticket or chargeback, and stops inactive domains hiding underpayment on active ones.

## Testing

7 new unit tests covering: a dedicated subscription still billing an inactive domain; an inactive domain's subscription no longer covering an active one; surplus from pooled domain billing; surplus from pooled inbox billing split across inactive domains; billing scheduled to end; surplus from the billing feature ledger; and groups where every domain is inactive. Audit, admin, renewal, cancel suites and the snapshot DB test (which applies the migration) also pass.

## Notes

* Expect some active domains to move from `paid` to `unpaid`/`underpaid` on the first run.
* When overcharge comes from pooled billing, which inactive domain carries it is arbitrary; the group total is correct.
* Not covered: billing for domains that have disappeared from CMR entirely (no finding row to attach it to).
* Rollback: revert the PR. The widened constraint is harmless if left in place.

Follows Acquisity/Acquisity#6595.

A customer cannot cancel a failed managed email domain and its still-active inboxes from Settings → Billing → Email Accounts & Domains because no Cancel button renders for domains in a failed provisioning state.

## Classification

Bug.

## What happened

* The Company Six workspace (org <uuid>) placed a DFY order (<uuid>) on 2026-05-01 for 2 domains, 3 inboxes each.
* <domain> was written as `failed` with error "Name 3 waiting for domain/mailboxes", but its 3 inboxes are `active` and `connected=true`.
* The billing card only renders a Cancel button for statuses `pending`/`active`/`partial` (apps/web/components/billing/email-accounts-domains-card.tsx), so the failed domain shows no Cancel option.

## Decision

Same outcome and root cause as the existing master ENG-13213 (DFY domain orders that fail leave names claimed and un-cancellable) and the ENG-12127 failed/error-state cancel gap. See the master for fix direction.

relatedSnapshot.title: DFY domain orders that fail leave names claimed and un-cancellable, blocking re-purchase and leaving the domain store inconsistent
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Root cause

When a Done-For-You domain order fails to provision at the provider, the domain rows are written to `mail_domain` (which has a global unique index `mail_domain_domain_unique` on `domain`) and left in a `failed` or `pending` state. Those rows are never released, so they keep holding the name for the original organization. A later order for the same name throws "Unable to claim domains for this organization" at the claim step, silently drops the overlapping domains, and leaves the new order stuck in `provisioning`.

Separately, a domain that failed still renders in Billing with no Cancel option, and the domain store availability check reads the registrar/provider (which never registered the failed name) instead of `mail_domain`. The result is a failed domain that shows as "available to purchase" while its name is actually still claimed internally.

## Evidence

* `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/mail/process-create-order.ts` `processCreateColdMailOrder`: claims domains into `mail_domain` (unique on `domain`), throws "Unable to claim domains for this organization: ..." when a name is already held, and on provider failure writes domains to `status='failed'` with the order left `requires_attention` or `provisioning`.
* `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/billing/reconcile-domain-orders-cron.ts`: retries failed inboxes on `requires_attention` orders, but does not release a domain name that failed at the provider and does not recover the duplicate-domain-claim collision.

## Blast radius (counted 2026-08-27)

Domain orders stuck in a non-terminal provisioning state: 17 `provisioning` across 17 organizations, 66 `requires_attention` across 66 organizations, 17 `failed` across 16 organizations. Done-For-You specifically: 3 `provisioning`, 26 `requires_attention`.

Domains in `failed` status with at least one `active` inbox (counted 2026-09-05): 106 domains across 41 organizations.

Paid `requires_attention` orders older than 7 days that hold `failed` domains (counted 2026-09-11): 26 orders across 25 organizations, holding 51 failed domains. Never-retried `error` inboxes on failed domains older than 7 days: 33, across 5 organizations. A 2026-09-10 count of the same cohort returned identical figures.

DFY orders stranded by a stale cross-organization `mail_domain` claim, with no saved provider order id and stale beyond 24 hours (counted 2026-09-23): 5 orders across 5 organizations and 5 users, from the ENG-14139 report. Collision cascade as of 2026-09-23: one stale failed claim is a foreign claim on 4 later DFY orders across 4 organizations, and pending claims written by two stuck orders block 4 further organizations' orders. The wider stuck-in-`provisioning` population is 9 orders across 9 organizations, of which 4 belong to ENG-13308's stall mechanism.

## Fix direction

* Release a failed domain's claim so the name can be re-purchased, and reconcile the domain store's availability check against owned-but-failed domains.
* Stop silently dropping overlapping domains from a new DFY order; fail fast with a clear message to the customer instead.

relatedSnapshot.title: Billing shows 18 purchased inboxes but Email Accounts shows 6; four of six DFY domains failed provisioning and stay billed and un-cancellable
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Testable claim

In the reported workspace, Billing -> Email Accounts & Domains lists 6 domains and 18 inboxes while Cold Email Agent -> Email Accounts lists only 6 inboxes, because four of the six Done-For-You domains (12 inboxes) failed provider provisioning and are still held in a requires_attention order, un-cancellable and still billed.

## Intercom conversation context

Reporter states (2026-09-10): the Billing settings show 6 domains with 3 emails each, but the campaign Email Accounts tab only shows 6. She expected 18, says office hours confirmed a bug, and shared screenshots. A campaign page also showed "No email accounts connected. Add one to start sending." on an Active campaign.
Conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

## Evidence

* Production: domain_purchase_order status requires_attention, completedAt null; 6 mail_domain rows in status failed ("Domain or mailbox provisioning failed"), provisionedAt null; 12 mail_inbox rows status error, connected false, retryCount 0, lastRetryAt null; 6 mail_inbox rows active/connected. Order created 2026-08-16.
* Name 13: billing.reconcile-domain-orders-cron runs every 30 minutes and still re-attempts the same unconnected inboxes; mail_inbox.retryCount never advances.
* Provider: Company Three account list for the workspace returns exactly 6 active accounts, matching the 6 provisioned inboxes.
* Help center: the Billing card is a domain/inbox billing view and is explicitly not a provisioning status panel, so the count difference itself is expected; the defect is the unresolved failed domains.

## Blast radius (counted 2026-09-10)

* 7 requires_attention orders across 6 organizations hold 22 failed domains.
* 33 unconnected, never-retried inboxes on failed domains older than 7 days, across 5 organizations.

## Suggested link

Overlaps the existing DFY failed-domain master family (failed domains left claimed, un-cancellable and still billed); dedupe and parent during routing.
